# 🧬 Comprehensive Research Report: `gatk.CalculateContamination`

---

## 1. Tool Purpose & Scientific Applications

### Overview
`CalculateContamination` is a core component of the **GATK4 (Genome Analysis Toolkit v4)** suite, developed and maintained by the **Broad Institute**. It estimates the fraction of reads in a sequenced sample that originate from cross-sample contamination, given pileup data generated by the upstream `GetPileupSummaries` tool.

### Scientific Role
Cross-sample contamination is one of the most common sources of artifact mutations in somatic variant calling. Even low levels of contamination (1–5%) can generate spurious somatic calls. `CalculateContamination` quantifies this contamination fraction using a **binomial mixture model** applied to germline variant sites from population databases (e.g., gnomAD), enabling downstream filtering by `FilterMutectCalls`.

### Algorithm
The tool uses **maximum likelihood estimation (MLE)** over germline heterozygous and homozygous variant sites:
- At sites where a sample is **homozygous reference**: contamination introduces alternate-allele reads at a frequency ≈ contamination fraction × population alt frequency
- At sites where a sample is **homozygous alternate**: contamination introduces reference reads
- The model integrates these observations genome-wide to produce a single contamination fraction estimate and its standard error
- When tumor **segmentation** is also output, the model accounts for allelic imbalance across aneuploid regions

### Applications
| Application | Description |
|---|---|
| **Somatic QC** | Primary QC gate in GATK Best Practices somatic pipeline |
| **Sample swap detection** | High contamination (>10%) may indicate sample mislabeling |
| **Tumor purity estimation** | Segmentation output reflects minor allele fractions across the genome |
| **Clinical variant interpretation** | Clean contamination estimates are required for clinical-grade variant calls |
| **Population-scale cohort QC** | Batch assessment of sample quality across cancer cohorts |

## 2. Input / Output Formats

### Inputs

| Parameter | Flag | Required | Format | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tumor pileup summary | `-I` / `--input` | ✅ Yes | `.table` (TSV) | Output of `GetPileupSummaries` on tumor sample |
| Matched normal pileup | `-matched` / `--matched-normal-input` | ❌ No | `.table` (TSV) | Output of `GetPileupSummaries` on matched normal; enables matched-normal mode |
| Arguments file | `--arguments_file` | ❌ No | Plain text | One additional argument per line |

#### Pileup Summary Table Format (`.table`)
```
contig  position  ref_count  alt_count  allele_frequency  other_alt_count
chr1    10146     20         0          0.36              1
chr1    10151     25         1          0.36              0
...
```

### Outputs

| Output | Flag | Required | Format | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Contamination table | `-O` / `--output` | ✅ Yes | `.table` (TSV) | Contamination fraction estimate + standard error |
| Tumor segmentation table | `--tumor-segmentation` | ❌ No | `.table` (TSV) | Minor allele fractions per genomic segment |

#### Contamination Table Format
```
sample              contamination  error
tumor_sample_name   0.0127         0.0031
```

#### Tumor Segmentation Table Format
```
contig  start     end       minor_allele_fraction
chr1    1         10000000  0.498
chr1    10000001  30000000  0.312
...
```

### Installation Methods
```bash
# 1. Docker (recommended for GenePattern)
docker pull broadinstitute/gatk:latest

# 2. Conda
conda create -n gatk4 -c bioconda -c conda-forge gatk4
conda activate gatk4

# 3. Direct JAR (GitHub Releases)
wget https://github.com/broadinstitute/gatk/releases/download/4.4.0.0/gatk-4.4.0.0.zip
unzip gatk-4.4.0.0.zip

# 4. Direct invocation with Java
java -jar gatk-package-4.4.0.0-local.jar CalculateContamination --help
```

### Invocation Methods
```bash
# Via gatk wrapper (Python script)
gatk CalculateContamination -I tumor.table -O contamination.table

# Via Java directly
java -jar gatk.jar CalculateContamination -I tumor.table -O contamination.table

# Via Docker
docker run -v $(pwd):/data broadinstitute/gatk:latest \
  gatk CalculateContamination -I /data/tumor.table -O /data/contamination.table
```

## 5. Common Workflows & Usage Patterns

### Complete GATK Somatic Best Practices Pipeline
```
[FASTQ] → BWA-MEM → [BAM] → MarkDuplicates → BQSR → [Recalibrated BAM]
                                                            ↓
                                                        Mutect2 → [Unfiltered VCF]
                                                            ↓
                                         GetPileupSummaries (tumor + optional normal)
                                                            ↓
                                          CalculateContamination ← [You Are Here]
                                                            ↓
                                    FilterMutectCalls (using contamination.table + segments.table)
                                                            ↓
                                                     [Filtered VCF]
```

### Mode 1: Tumor-Only
```bash
gatk CalculateContamination \
  -I tumor_pileup_summaries.table \
  -O contamination.table \
  --tumor-segmentation tumor_segments.table
```

### Mode 2: Matched Normal (preferred when available)
```bash
gatk CalculateContamination \
  -I tumor_pileup_summaries.table \
  -matched normal_pileup_summaries.table \
  -O contamination.table \
  --tumor-segmentation tumor_segments.table
```

## 6. Python Wrapper Script for GenePattern

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
GenePattern Module Wrapper: gatk.CalculateContamination
========================================================
Wraps the GATK4 CalculateContamination tool for cross-sample contamination
estimation. Supports both tumor-only and matched normal modes.

Author:    GenePattern Module Development
Tool:      GATK CalculateContamination (Broad Institute)
GATK Docs: https://gatk.broadinstitute.org/hc/en-us/articles/360036888972
"""

import argparse
import logging
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

# ── Logging setup ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
logging.basicConfig(
    level=logging.INFO,
    format="[%(asctime)s] %(levelname)s: %(message)s",
    datefmt="%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S",
    stream=sys.stdout,
)
log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


# ── Helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _resolve_gatk() -> str:
    """
    Locate the GATK executable.
    Search order:
      1. GATK_PATH environment variable (full path to 'gatk' script or JAR)
      2. 'gatk' on the PATH
      3. Common installation locations
    Returns the command prefix (e.g. 'gatk' or 'java -jar /path/to/gatk.jar').
    """
    # 1. Environment variable override
    gatk_env = os.environ.get("GATK_PATH", "").strip()
    if gatk_env:
        if gatk_env.endswith(".jar"):
            java_bin = os.environ.get("JAVA_HOME", "")
            java_cmd = os.path.join(java_bin, "bin", "java") if java_bin else "java"
            log.info("Using GATK JAR (from GATK_PATH): %s", gatk_env)
            return f"{java_cmd} -jar {gatk_env}"
        else:
            log.info("Using GATK executable (from GATK_PATH): %s", gatk_env)
            return gatk_env

    # 2. 'gatk' on PATH
    import shutil
    if shutil.which("gatk"):
        log.info("Using 'gatk' found on PATH.")
        return "gatk"

    # 3. Common fallback locations
    fallbacks = [
        "/opt/gatk/gatk",
        "/usr/local/bin/gatk",
        "/gatk/gatk",           # Docker image default
    ]
    for path in fallbacks:
        if os.path.isfile(path):
            log.info("Using GATK at fallback path: %s", path)
            return path

    raise FileNotFoundError(
        "GATK executable not found. Set the GATK_PATH environment variable "
        "to the full path of the 'gatk' wrapper script or the GATK JAR file."
    )


def _validate_input_file(filepath: str, label: str) -> Path:
    """Validate that a required input file exists and is non-empty."""
    p = Path(filepath)
    if not p.exists():
        log.error("%s not found: %s", label, filepath)
        sys.exit(1)
    if p.stat().st_size == 0:
        log.error("%s is empty: %s", label, filepath)
        sys.exit(1)
    log.info("Validated %s: %s", label, p.resolve())
    return p


def _validate_optional_file(filepath: str | None, label: str) -> Path | None:
    """Validate an optional input file if it was provided."""
    if not filepath:
        return None
    return _validate_input_file(filepath, label)


def _ensure_output_dir(filepath: str) -> None:
    """Create parent directories for an output file path if they don't exist."""
    parent = Path(filepath).parent
    if parent and not parent.exists():
        log.info("Creating output directory: %s", parent)
        parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)


def _run_command(cmd: list[str]) -> int:
    """
    Execute a shell command, streaming stdout/stderr to the logger.
    Returns the exit code.
    """
    cmd_str = " ".join(cmd)
    log.info("Running command:\n  %s", cmd_str)
    print(f"\n{'='*72}", flush=True)
    print(f"COMMAND: {cmd_str}", flush=True)
    print(f"{'='*72}\n", flush=True)

    proc = subprocess.Popen(
        cmd,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
        text=True,
        bufsize=1,
    )
    assert proc.stdout is not None
    for line in proc.stdout:
        print(line, end="", flush=True)
    proc.wait()
    return proc.returncode


# ── Argument parsing ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _build_arg_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="gatk_calculate_contamination",
        description=(
            "GenePattern wrapper for GATK CalculateContamination.\n\n"
            "Estimates cross-sample contamination from pileup summaries generated "
            "by GetPileupSummaries. Supports tumor-only mode and matched normal mode."
        ),
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
        epilog="""
EXAMPLES
--------
# Tumor-only mode (minimal)
  python gatk_calculate_contamination.py \\
      --tumor-pileup-input  tumor_pileup_summary.table \\
      --output              contamination.table

# Tumor-only mode with segmentation output
  python gatk_calculate_contamination.py \\
      --tumor-pileup-input      tumor_pileup_summary.table \\
      --output                  contamination.table \\
      --tumor-segmentation-output tumor_segments.table

# Matched normal mode
  python gatk_calculate_contamination.py \\
      --tumor-pileup-input      tumor_pileup_summary.table \\
      --matched-normal-input    normal_pileup_summary.table \\
      --output                  contamination.table \\
      --tumor-segmentation-output tumor_segments.table

# With additional arguments file
  python gatk_calculate_contamination.py \\
      --tumor-pileup-input  tumor_pileup_summary.table \\
      --output              contamination.table \\
      --arguments-file      extra_gatk_args.txt

NOTES
-----
- Input .table files MUST be produced by GATK GetPileupSummaries.
- When --matched-normal-input is provided, matched-normal mode is used
  (more accurate). Without it, tumor-only mode is used.
- Output files are consumed by GATK FilterMutectCalls:
    --contamination-table  <contamination.table>
    --tumor-segmentation   <tumor_segments.table>
- Set GATK_PATH env variable to override GATK executable location.
""",
    )

    # ── Required parameters ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
    req = parser.add_argument_group("Required Parameters")
    req.add_argument(
        "--tumor-pileup-input",
        metavar="FILE",
        required=True,
        help=(
            "Tumor pileup summary table (.table) produced by GATK GetPileupSummaries. "
            "Tab-delimited file with columns: contig, position, ref_count, alt_count, "
            "allele_frequency, other_alt_count. [REQUIRED]"
        ),
    )
    req.add_argument(
        "--output",
        metavar="FILE",
        required=True,
        help=(
            "Output contamination table (.table). Tab-delimited file with columns: "
            "sample, contamination, error. Contamination is a fraction between 0 and 1. "
            "[REQUIRED]"
        ),
    )

    # ── Optional parameters ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
    opt = parser.add_argument_group("Optional Parameters")
    opt.add_argument(
        "--matched-normal-input",
        metavar="FILE",
        default=None,
        help=(
            "Matched normal pileup summary table (.table) from GetPileupSummaries. "
            "When provided, enables MATCHED NORMAL MODE for more accurate contamination "
            "estimation. When omitted, TUMOR-ONLY MODE is used. "
            "GATK flag: -matched / --matched-normal-input. [OPTIONAL]"
        ),
    )
    opt.add_argument(
        "--tumor-segmentation-output",
        metavar="FILE",
        default=None,
        help=(
            "Output file for tumor segmentation table (.table). Contains minor allele "
            "fractions per genomic segment (columns: contig, start, end, "
            "minor_allele_fraction). Required input for GATK FilterMutectCalls "
            "(--tumor-segmentation flag). GATK flag: --tumor-segmentation. [OPTIONAL]"
        ),
    )
    opt.add_argument(
        "--arguments-file",
        metavar="FILE",
        default=None,
        help=(
            "Text file containing additional GATK arguments, one per line. "
            "Use this to pass advanced or common GATK arguments such as: "
            "--verbosity INFO, --TMP_DIR /tmp, --QUIET, --gcs-max-retries 30, etc. "
            "GATK flag: --arguments_file. [OPTIONAL]"
        ),
    )

    return parser


# ── Command builder ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def _build_gatk_command(
    gatk_cmd: str,
    tumor_pileup_input: str,
    output: str,
    matched_normal_input: str | None,
    tumor_segmentation_output: str | None,
    arguments_file: str | None,
) -> list[str]:
    """
    Assemble the full GATK CalculateContamination command as a list of tokens.
    The gatk_cmd may be a multi-word string (e.g. 'java -jar /path/to/gatk.jar'),
    which is why we split it.
    """
    cmd = gatk_cmd.split() + ["CalculateContamination"]

    # Required
    cmd += ["-I", tumor_pileup_input]
    cmd += ["-O", output]

    # Matched normal (optional) — triggers matched-normal mode
    if matched_normal_input:
        cmd += ["-matched", matched_normal_input]

    # Tumor segmentation output (optional)
    if tumor_segmentation_output:
        cmd += ["--tumor-segmentation", tumor_segmentation_output]

    # Additional arguments file (optional)
    if arguments_file:
        cmd += ["--arguments_file", arguments_file]

    return cmd


# ── Main entrypoint ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    parser = _build_arg_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    log.info("=" * 72)
    log.info("gatk.CalculateContamination — GenePattern Module Wrapper")
    log.info("=" * 72)

    # ── Determine operating mode ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    mode = "MATCHED NORMAL" if args.matched_normal_input else "TUMOR-ONLY"
    log.info("Operating mode: %s", mode)

    # ── Validate inputs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    _validate_input_file(args.tumor_pileup_input, "Tumor pileup summary")
    _validate_optional_file(args.matched_normal_input, "Matched normal pileup summary")
    _validate_optional_file(args.arguments_file, "Additional arguments file")

    # ── Ensure output directories exist ──────────────────────────────────────
    _ensure_output_dir(args.output)
    if args.tumor_segmentation_output:
        _ensure_output_dir(args.tumor_segmentation_output)

    # ── Locate GATK ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    try:
        gatk_cmd = _resolve_gatk()
    except FileNotFoundError as exc:
        log.error(str(exc))
        sys.exit(1)

    # ── Build and run command ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
    cmd = _build_gatk_command(
        gatk_cmd=gatk_cmd,
        tumor_pileup_input=args.tumor_pileup_input,
        output=args.output,
        matched_normal_input=args.matched_normal_input,
        tumor_segmentation_output=args.tumor_segmentation_output,
        arguments_file=args.arguments_file,
    )

    exit_code = _run_command(cmd)

    # ── Post-run validation ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
    if exit_code != 0:
        log.error("GATK CalculateContamination failed with exit code %d.", exit_code)
        sys.exit(exit_code)

    log.info("GATK CalculateContamination completed successfully.")

    # ── Report outputs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    _report_output(args.output, "Contamination table")
    if args.tumor_segmentation_output:
        _report_output(args.tumor_segmentation_output, "Tumor segmentation table")

    log.info("=" * 72)
    log.info("Module execution complete.")
    log.info("=" * 72)


def _report_output(filepath: str, label: str) -> None:
    """Log a summary of a produced output file."""
    p = Path(filepath)
    if p.exists() and p.stat().st_size > 0:
        # Show the first few lines for user feedback
        try:
            with open(p) as fh:
                header = fh.readline().strip()
                first_data = fh.readline().strip()
            log.info(
                "%s written: %s  (%d bytes)",
                label, p.resolve(), p.stat().st_size,
            )
            log.info("  Header : %s", header)
            if first_data:
                log.info("  Row 1  : %s", first_data)
        except Exception:
            log.info("%s written: %s", label, p.resolve())
    else:
        log.warning(
            "%s not found or empty after execution: %s", label, filepath
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

## 8. Comparative Analysis

| Feature | `CalculateContamination` | `VerifyBamID2` | `Conpair` |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Input** | Pileup summary table (.table) | BAM directly | BAM directly |
| **Reference panel** | User-supplied (gnomAD) | Built-in 1000G panels | User-supplied |
| **Matched normal mode** | ✅ Yes | ❌ No | ✅ Yes |
| **Pipeline integration** | GATK Best Practices native | Standalone | Standalone |
| **Tumor segmentation output** | ✅ Yes | ❌ No | ❌ No |
| **FilterMutectCalls integration** | ✅ Native | ❌ No | ❌ No |
| **Cloud (GCS) support** | ✅ Yes | ❌ No | ❌ No |
| **Preprocessing required** | GetPileupSummaries | None | None |
| **Typical runtime** | Seconds | Minutes | Minutes |

**Key advantages of `CalculateContamination`:** Natively integrated into the GATK somatic pipeline, produces segmentation output required by `FilterMutectCalls`, extremely fast (operates on pre-computed pileup tables not raw BAMs), and supports cloud storage.

---

## 9. Known Limitations & Caveats

| Issue | Description | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| **Input dependency** | Requires pileup summaries from `GetPileupSummaries`; generic pileup formats not accepted | Always run GetPileupSummaries first |
| **Reference panel sensitivity** | Accuracy depends on quality of germline resource used in GetPileupSummaries | Use high-quality panel (e.g., gnomAD) |
| **Low coverage** | Sparse pileup tables (few sites) reduce estimation accuracy | Ensure adequate read depth and broad interval list |
| **Tumor-only accuracy** | Less accurate than matched-normal mode for distinguishing germline from contamination | Use matched normal whenever possible |
| **Highly aneuploid tumors** | Extreme copy number changes can bias tumor-only estimates | Use `--tumor-segmentation` output for `FilterMutectCalls` |
| **FFPE samples** | Oxidative damage artifacts may inflate contamination estimate | Use strand-specific filters and FFPE-aware variant calling |

planning_data.plan:
# GATK.CalculateContamination — GenePattern Module Plan

## 1. Module Identity & Purpose
- **Module Name**: GATK.CalculateContamination
- **Tool**: GATK4 CalculateContamination (Broad Institute)
- **Version**: 4.1.4.1 (Docker: broadinstitute/gatk:4.1.4.1)
- **Language**: Python (wrapper) / Java (underlying GATK tool)
- **Author**: GenePattern Team
- **LSID**: urn:lsid:broad.mit.edu:cancer.software.genepattern.module.generated:93475:1

## 2. Scientific Purpose
CalculateContamination estimates the fraction of reads in a sequenced tumor sample that originate from cross-sample contamination. Using pileup summaries previously generated by GetPileupSummaries, the tool applies a binomial mixture model via maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) over germline variant sites. The resulting contamination fraction estimate and per-segment minor allele fractions are consumed by FilterMutectCalls to remove contamination artifacts from somatic variant calls.

## 3. Operating Modes
- **Tumor-Only Mode** (default): Only the tumor pileup summary is provided. Less accurate but always available.
- **Matched Normal Mode** (preferred): Both tumor and matched normal pileup summaries are provided. The wrapper detects the mode automatically based on whether `matched.normal.input` is supplied.

## 4. Parameter Design

### Exposed GenePattern Parameters (5 total)

| Parameter Name | Type | Required | Default | GATK Flag |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| tumor.pileup.input | File | Yes | — | -I / --input |
| output | Text | Yes | contamination.table | -O / --output |
| matched.normal.input | File | No | — | -matched / --matched-normal-input |
| tumor.segmentation.output | Text | No | — | --tumor-segmentation |
| arguments.file | File | No | — | --arguments_file |

### Intentionally Excluded Parameters
Per design instructions, the following categories are NOT exposed as GenePattern parameters. Users may pass them via arguments.file:
- Optional tool arguments: --low-count-filter-threshold, --minimum-base-quality, etc.
- Common GATK arguments: --gatk-config-file, --gcs-max-retries, --gcs-project-for-requester-pays, --QUIET, --TMP_DIR, --verbosity, --use-jdk-deflater, --use-jdk-inflater
- Advanced arguments: any internal GATK advanced options

## 5. Wrapper Script Architecture (gatk_calculate_contamination_wrapper.py)

### Design Principles
- Written in Python 3 using argparse for parameter parsing
- Auto-detects operating mode (tumor-only vs matched normal) based on presence of matched.normal.input
- Resolves GATK executable via: (1) GATK_PATH env var, (2) 'gatk' on PATH, (3) common fallback paths including /gatk/gatk for Docker
- Validates all input files exist and are non-empty before invoking GATK
- Auto-creates parent directories for output files
- Streams GATK stdout/stderr to GenePattern log
- Reports output file paths, sizes, header lines, and first data rows
- Propagates GATK exit codes faithfully

### Command Structure
```
python <libdir>gatk_calculate_contamination_wrapper.py \
    --tumor-pileup-input <tumor.pileup.input> \
    --output <output> \
    [--matched-normal-input <matched.normal.input>] \
    [--tumor-segmentation-output <tumor.segmentation.output>] \
    [--arguments-file <arguments.file>]
```

The wrapper builds the GATK invocation as:
```
gatk CalculateContamination \
    -I tumor.table \
    -O contamination.table \
    [-matched normal.table] \
    [--tumor-segmentation segments.table] \
    [--arguments_file extra_args.txt]
```

## 6. Input/Output Specification

### Inputs
- **tumor.pileup.input**: .table TSV from GetPileupSummaries (columns: contig, position, ref_count, alt_count, allele_frequency, other_alt_count)
- **matched.normal.input**: .table TSV from GetPileupSummaries on matched normal sample (same format)
- **arguments.file**: Plain text file, one GATK argument per line

### Outputs
- **contamination.table** (named by `output` parameter): TSV with columns sample, contamination, error
- **tumor segments table** (named by `tumor.segmentation.output` parameter): TSV with columns contig, start, end, minor_allele_fraction

## 7. Docker Environment
- **Image**: broadinstitute/gatk:4.1.4.1
- GATK executable available at /gatk/gatk in the image
- Java runtime bundled within the image
- Python 3 available for running the wrapper

## 8. Resource Requirements
- **CPU**: 1 core (CalculateContamination is single-threaded)
- **Memory**: 4 GB (JVM + pileup table processing)
- **Runtime**: Typically seconds to minutes depending on pileup table size

## 9. Parameter Groups (UI Organization)
1. **Required Inputs**: tumor.pileup.input, output
2. **Optional Inputs (Matched Normal Mode)**: matched.normal.input
3. **Optional Outputs**: tumor.segmentation.output
4. **Advanced**: arguments.file

## 10. Pipeline Context
This module fits into the GATK Somatic Best Practices pipeline:
GetPileupSummaries (tumor) → CalculateContamination → FilterMutectCalls
GetPileupSummaries (normal) ↗

## 11. Validation Strategy
1. Confirm tumor.pileup.input exists and is non-empty
2. If matched.normal.input provided, confirm it exists and is non-empty
3. If arguments.file provided, confirm it exists
4. Verify GATK is accessible in the Docker environment
5. Confirm output files are produced with non-zero size after execution
6. Log header and first data row of each output for user feedback

## 12. Testing Approach
- **Tumor-only**: Run with tumor_pileup_summary.table only
- **Matched normal**: Run with both tumor_pileup_summary.table and normal_pileup_summary.table
- **With segmentation**: Confirm tumor segmentation output is produced when tumor.segmentation.output is specified
- **With arguments.file**: Pass additional arguments and confirm GATK receives them
- **Error handling**: Test with missing/empty input files to confirm meaningful error messages
- **Exit code**: Test that non-zero GATK exit codes cause the wrapper to exit with the same code

parameters.name: tumor.pileup.input
parameters.description: Tumor pileup summary table (.table) produced by GATK GetPileupSummaries. Tab-delimited file with columns: contig, position, ref_count, alt_count, allele_frequency, other_alt_count. This is the primary required input for contamination estimation. GATK flag: -I / --input.

parameters.name: output
parameters.description: Name of the output contamination table file. The output is a tab-delimited .table file with columns: sample, contamination, error. The contamination value is a fraction between 0 and 1. This file is consumed by FilterMutectCalls via --contamination-table. GATK flag: -O / --output.

parameters.name: matched.normal.input
parameters.description: Matched normal pileup summary table (.table) from GetPileupSummaries run on the paired normal sample. When provided, enables MATCHED NORMAL MODE for more accurate contamination estimation. When omitted, TUMOR-ONLY MODE is used. Matched normal mode is strongly preferred when a paired normal is available. GATK flag: -matched / --matched-normal-input.

parameters.name: tumor.segmentation.output
parameters.description: Output filename for the tumor segmentation table. Contains minor allele fractions per genomic segment with columns: contig, start, end, minor_allele_fraction. This output is consumed by FilterMutectCalls via --tumor-segmentation. Highly recommended for aneuploid tumors to account for allelic imbalance. GATK flag: --tumor-segmentation.

parameters.name: arguments.file
parameters.description: Text file containing additional GATK arguments, one argument per line. Use this to pass optional, common, or advanced GATK options that are not exposed as GenePattern parameters — for example: --verbosity INFO, --TMP_DIR /tmp, --QUIET, --gcs-max-retries 30, --gatk-config-file myconfig.config, --use-jdk-deflater, --use-jdk-inflater. GATK flag: --arguments_file.
